provenance_note: Mined from the same MIT-licensed sage3648/mythicsim-forever-engine repository as the spell data pack. Items/enchants: data/items.jsonl and data/enchants.jsonl (the real client item database - this engine's gems.jsonl is empty; Forever's own item.rs explicitly refuses an equipped gem since 'the database has none of' - gems are genuinely not modeled in the source engine itself, not a gap in this mining pass). Rating-to-percent conversions: src/prepare/character.rs's constants module (exact values, not estimated). Haste: src/mechanics/haste.rs's cast_speed formula. Race base stats and the Warlock Intellect-to-crit conversion: data/go-tables.json (itself mined from the Go reference engine's core.BaseStats and crit-per-int tables). known_conflicts and unimplemented_but_parsed below record what this pack carries but this engine does not yet apply.
unimplemented_but_parsed: pseudo_stats (an alternate percentage-based stat representation some items/enchants carry instead of a flat rating, confirmed present on 23 rows of the source engine's full data/items.jsonl) and item set bonuses (set_id/set_name, present on 10038 Stormcloth Shoulders among this pack's own mined items - part of the 6-piece 'Stormcloth Regalia' set, confirmed by re-fetching data/items.jsonl directly on 2026-10-24 and grepping for set_id=1972) are real client-data concepts this mining pass's flattening step (name/slot/stats only) drops before they ever reach this JSON - not something gear.rs fails to parse, something the pack itself never carries. Checked and confirmed inert for every item/build in this pack specifically: none of the 17 mined items carry a nonzero pseudo_stat, and no example build here equips more than one Stormcloth piece (10038 alone, never with any of its five set-mates: 10010/10011/10020/10032/10039), so no set bonus is actually live to silently drop. Would need re-mining with the flattening step changed to carry these through, not a gear.rs fix, if a future item/build needs them.

random_suffix / rand_prop_points ("of the Whatever" randomly-enchanted items, i.e. a non-zero `scaling_options[*].rand_prop_points` in the source `data/items.jsonl`): three of this pack's 17 mined items have it (10038 Stormcloth Shoulders: 15, 14153 Robe of the Void: 45, 14146 Gloves of Spell Mastery: 34, re-confirmed directly against the source JSONL on 2026-10-24) but none of the real 'builder starter' request fixtures this pack's example builds are taken from ever actually chose a suffix for them, so it's currently inert, not silently wrong - but ItemRow has no field for it at all, so a future item that DOES need a chosen suffix can't be represented without a gear.rs/ItemRow change.

item_effects (on-equip procs and on-use trinket effects): only one of this pack's 17 mined items has any (14153 Robe of the Void: a 'Heal Pet' on-use effect, buff_id 18386, 600s cooldown - re-confirmed directly against the source JSONL on 2026-10-24) and it's a pet-health utility effect with no damage component, outside this engine's DPS-only scope regardless (there's no pet-health mechanic to heal). No damage proc is silently dropped by any item in this pack today, but ItemRow still has no field for item_effects at all, so a future item with a real damage proc would need one added, not just populated.

ShadowDamage/FireDamage and Intellect-to-mana, both listed here as unimplemented in this pack's rev2: both were actually implemented in gear.rs's rev2-era code (bonus_shadow_power/bonus_fire_power split, and the -280 + 15/Intellect mana formula from wowsims/forever's sim/core/mana.go) - this field just wasn't updated to say so at the time. Corrected in rev3; see gear.rs's own module doc for the current, accurate list of what is and isn't modeled.

rating_conversions._source: src/prepare/character.rs constants + src/mechanics/haste.rs (SPELL_HASTE_RATING_PER_PERCENT_TIMES_100=1000.0, i.e. 10 rating/1%, derived not copy-pasted).
rating_conversions._unify_gear_hit_and_crit: Forever's own rule (forever_rules.go unifyGearHitAndCrit, read via src/prepare/items.rs): a gear set's melee and spell hit ratings are summed into one percent and reapplied to BOTH; same for crit. gear.rs implements this - a caster's gear-granted melee hit/crit (from an off-type item) genuinely does count as spell hit/crit here, it isn't a mining error.

destruction_reference._source: validation/2026-10-06-warlock-multi-target-census/bases/2-targets/destruction-warlock.request.json's equipment list - a real fixture build, not hand-assembled.
